messages:
Alejandra: Heads up — noticed a small batch of sampled request/response logs this morning that still contain raw email addresses for a handful of requests. Only ~12 traces so far.
Sam: 😬 which routes? any pattern on tenant or region?
Alejandra: All from /v1/generate-chat and hitting the quota-attenuation routing. Region: eu-west-1. Tenants are a mix (two prod, one staging). Link to the rollouts page: https://console.redwood.ai/rollouts/qa
Mike: Is this the change where we started forwarding low-priority debug captures to the minidaemon in the canary pool? I thought we applied the pre-scrub hook there.
Alejandra: That was the idea. The scrub hook ran but our regex for email in attachments missed some of the multipart payloads. Example raw snippet we saw:
```json
{"resp_body": "Customer reached out: hi@acme.co
More text..."}
```
Jess: Oof. Is this coming from an older client that sends attachments as base64? we had a known edge-case where base64 parts skip the normal scrub path.
Sam: Good call — I remember codepath: attachments are streamed into an ingest buffer and then routed. The scrub step is in the structured-parse pipeline; streaming path may bypass it if size > 1MB.
Mike: Repro steps I tried locally: send a request with a base64-encoded HTML attachment containing an email, route through quota-attenuation config. The inspect hook was not called because the chunked stream was marked `large=true` so it took the fast-path.
Alejandra: Workaround for now: disable forwarding to canary for quota-attenuation for eu-west-1 until we ship the fix. Any objections? It's ~5% of debug traffic.
Jess: +1 — prefer quick rollback than leak risk. Can we add a temporary sampling filter so we don't capture full bodies for those tenants instead of full rollback?
Sam: We can set `inspect.capture_level = meta_only` for the affected route/tenants, that should avoid body capture while keeping headers/traces.
Mike: Will that change affect our ability to debug throughput regressions from the canary? we lose payloads but keep timing/provenance.
Alejandra: Acceptable tradeoff for the window. I opened a ticket: https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4829 with reproduction, stack traces and proposed fix.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: rollback quota-attenuation-forwarding eu-west-1 canary -> 1736502400 (ETA 20m). :gear:
Sam: For the real fix: we should ensure the scrub hook runs in both streaming and fast-path chunking. Proposed patch: move the scrub call earlier in the ingest pipeline and run base64 inspect on attachments before routing. Also add unit tests for multipart base64.
Jess: Also add an integration test that simulates the sample pipeline — we missed this in the rollout tests.
Mike: I'll start the patch. Plan: (1) small refactor to call scrub in stream head, (2) add size-guarded buffer to sanity-check attachments for email-like patterns, (3) add e2e harness test that runs against minidaemon canary routing.
Alejandra: ETA for patch/PR?
Mike: I'll aim for a PR by EOD and request review from Sam/Jess.
Sam: I'll add a temporary dashboard alert: any sampled log that contains `@` in the body will trigger a pager for 30m window so we can catch regressions during rollout.
Alejandra: Thanks all. After rollback and patch, let's do a targeted canary with a single tenant and 1% sample before full restore.
Jess: Agree. Also update the rollout doc with the sampling caveat so SREs know where to look.
Alejandra: Filing follow-ups in the ticket. FYI — we should also audit other forwarding policies (burst-routing, debug-burst) for the same fast-path gap.
Sam: noted. I'll add checklist items. Closing thread after rollback completes.
